title: Arkret Seal
description: Wire shape of a Arkret CBA Seal. It finalizes only control-plane Events. `delta[]` is the canonical set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal; cumulative coverage is derived recursively as covered_set(S)=set(S.delta) union covered_set(predecessor_refs[]). `control_event_set_root` authenticates that recursive covered_set and is used for basis, inclusion and non-membership proofs. Optional data_* roots are observational only and MUST NOT gate DataEvents. Identity & signature model (see zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6): the typed `id` (`ak:seal:<algo>:<hex>`) is content-derived — its hex equals H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Seal canonical bytes are the canonical JSON of every signed top-level field EXCEPT id and notary_signature. The `notary_signature` is NOT part of canonical bytes. Receivers MUST recompute H(seal_canonical_bytes) and verify the notary signature over the same bytes.

id.description: Content-derived typed reference. hex part MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm, where seal_canonical_bytes is the canonical JSON of every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`. Receivers MUST recompute and verify; mismatch → digest_mismatch. NEVER include `id` in the hash input — that would create a self-reference.

delta.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal. DataEvent digests MUST NOT appear here. Receivers MUST reject the Seal if any delta entry is already covered by a predecessor, if any entry is not a known valid Control Move digest, or if the list is not canonical sorted and duplicate-free.

control_event_set_root.description: Authenticated root over the recursive covered_set of this Seal. Default construction is RFC6962 Merkle root over canonical bytewise-sorted covered_set(S); inclusion uses Merkle audit path and non-membership uses sorted-neighbor proof. The root is not computed over delta[] alone.

state_root.description: Merkle root of control-plane cell state only.

completeness_root.description: Control-plane per-actor interval / chain-head completeness commitment. It does not prove absence of unknown actors.

notary_seq.description: Per-signer or committee slot sequence used for equivocation detection. Same signer and same realm_id MUST NOT sign two different canonical Seal bodies with the same notary_seq.

data_view_root.description: Optional observational root of KeyView records keyed by data cell id. It is not a DataEvent admission gate.

data_event_set_root.description: Optional observational root over DataEvent digests seen in this seal window. Missing DataEvents are not invalid.

coverage_scope.description: Optional observational coverage declaration for data_view_root / data_event_set_root. The object is intentionally closed only by deployment profiles; core verifiers treat it as signed diagnostic material.

covered_event_digests.description: Optional compaction materialization of the full recursive covered_set(S), canonical bytewise-sorted and duplicate-free. When present, receivers MUST verify it equals set(delta) union all predecessor covered sets and that control_event_set_root is computed over this exact set. Non-compaction Seals normally omit it.

previous_state_root.description: Hash-algorithm transition only: present iff this Seal is a Transition Seal under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. When present, MUST be computed with the previous digest_algorithm algorithm over the same recursive covered_set as state_root, and MUST equal the receiver-recomputed root under that algorithm before the new state_root is accepted. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

previous_digest_algorithm.description: Profile id of the previous hash algorithm. Required iff previous_state_root is present; absent on non-transition Seals.

notary_signature.description: Signature over seal_canonical_bytes (every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`). MUST NOT enter the canonical bytes itself — signatures never sign themselves. Seal is not an Event Envelope, so its signature uses the generic non-Event proof field `payload_digest`; that value MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Event Envelope proofs use `event_digest` instead.

sealed_at.description: Wall-clock timestamp at which the notary signed this Seal. Used only for reducer-derived projection timestamps and freshness diagnostics; not a lattice winner input.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Bare DID is not valid for signatures because verifiers need a stable verification method, not only a controller DID.

payload_digest.description: Hash of seal_canonical_bytes for this non-Event Seal signature. Do not rename to event_digest: event_digest is reserved for Event Envelope proofs.
